attempts.raw_response: Gradually add the remaining sugar, a spoonful at a time, while continuing to beat on medium speed. Once all the sugar has been incorporated, increase the speed to medium-high and beat until you reach stiff, glossy peaks. At this stage, the whites should stand upright when you lift the beaters, and the texture should be smooth and shiny, not dry or grainy. Be careful not to overbeat, as the whites will become clumpy and difficult to fold into your batter. If you notice the mixture starting to look curdled or dull, stop immediately — you've gone too far. Properly beaten whites are light, airy, and hold their shape without slipping, providing the structure your recipe needs.

pair.human_continuation: Mix the remaining half of the sugar into the egg yolks in a separate bowl. Beat the mixture with a whisk until it is well blended. Gently fold the egg yolks into the beaten egg whites using a spatula, pouring slowly. The goal is to keep the fluffiness of the whites, which means you can stir too quickly or press too hard. Slowly pour the rum into the egg mixture, gently folding it in with your spatula. If you're serving the eggnog to children or prefer non-alcoholic eggnog, you can leave out the alcohol. Next, add the milk and half of the cream slowly to the bowl, gently stirring them in.  Start with 4 cups (1 L) of milk, then add more later to adjust the consistency.
pair.prefix: Using an electric beater set on medium speed, beat the egg whites until they turn white and frothy. Add half the sugar and beat just until soft peaks begin to form.  You can technically use a whisk instead of an electric beater, but the process will take more time and energy. "Soft peaks" should just begin to hold their form when you remove the mixer, but they'll melt back into the whites after a second or two.
